decision.explanation: The provided evidence from pmid-20560986 describes a patient with a novel VHL missense mutation (X214L, corresponding to c.641G>T) who presented with synchronous primary tumors including a pheochromocytoma and a malignant neuroendocrine tumor of the pancreas. The study also notes a family history of early-onset pheochromocytomas and screening revealed bilateral retinal hemangioblastomas (retinal capillary hemangioma). The authors explicitly state that analysis of this mutation supported the Type 2A phenotype of VHL disease. The claim specifies the variant VHL *214L (c.641G>T), the disease von Hippel-Lindau disease, and phenotypes including Pheochromocytoma, Retinal capillary hemangioma, and Pancreatic endocrine tumor. The evidence directly links the specific variant to the disease and the listed phenotypes, supporting the claim that this variant is associated with these manifestations in the context of VHL predisposition.

citations.quote: We report the clinical characteristics and functional consequences of a novel VHL, missense, mutation (X214L). Analysis of this mutation supported the Type 2A phenotype in families with a previously unclassifiable molecular subtype of VHL disease. . . . 20-year-old female referred for cancer genetics consultation due to a personal history of two synchronous primary tumors (a second primary pheochromocytoma and a malignant neuroendocrine tumor of the pancreas) and a family history of early-onset pheochromocytomas. . . . Screening for VHL-associated tumors revealed bilateral retinal HB
